processing: An unoxidised green, finished mainly by baking with some pan-firing; the maofeng shape is a lightly twisted downy leaf.
harvest_season: Spring. It belongs to the Wenzhou early tea group, so it reaches market early compared with northern Zhejiang.
appearance_dry: As is typical of maofeng greens, slender lightly curled shoots with visible down.
appearance_liquor: As is typical of maofeng greens, clear and bright yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Tender, whole shoots of a soft green, as with other maofeng teas.
taste_profile: Described as quietly fragrant and sweet, with the fresh tenderness associated with Wenzhou early teas.

brewing.notes: Treat it like other maofeng: a glass or gaiwan, water below the boil, and a short first steep.

vintage_note: Sold as the current spring's harvest, as is usual for Zhejiang greens, and best drunk within the year. Its place among the Wenzhou early teas means first lots arrive early and carry a premium.
description:
Yandang Maofeng comes from the Yandang mountains in Yueqing, on the Wenzhou coast. It is one of the county teas grouped under the Wenzhou early tea name, and a scenic-mountain tea in the classic Chinese sense, grown among volcanic rock and mist.

It is made with mostly baked drying and a touch of pan-firing. Exact grades and methods are little documented, but as with other maofeng teas, the style favours whole tender shoots with their down intact.

The usual description is a quiet fragrance and clean sweetness. Keep the water under the boil and expect delicacy rather than strength.

Buy it as a dated spring tea from Yueqing and be a little wary of the word maofeng on its own, since it covers many teas, Huangshan's being the most famous.
history:
Accounts of tea on Yandang reach back to the Eastern Jin and link it with the monk Nuojuna, and they place Yandang tea on a tribute list in 993. These dates come from later retellings and should be taken with caution.

The tea has more solid modern recognition: it received a national agricultural geographical indication in 2018, and it now appears among the county brands of Wenzhou early tea.
